title: Accenture to Strengthen Capabilities for Software and Automation Solutions from Siemens Digital Industries with Acquisition of Industries eXcellence Group
snippet: “Manufacturers are increasingly investing in software, data and AI to make engineering and factory operations more flexible, intelligent and connected,” said Tracey Countryman, global supply chain and...
fullText:
“Manufacturers are increasingly investing in software, data and AI to make engineering and factory operations more flexible, intelligent and connected,” said Tracey Countryman, global supply chain and engineering lead at Accenture. “But many companies struggle to integrate these technologies across their products, factories, plants and supply chains. We will combine IndX’s proven expertise in Siemens technologies with Accenture’s AI capabilities and industry knowledge to solve this challenge for clients faster.”

        

Headquartered in Rome and Chicago, IndX brings proven expertise in software for discrete and process manufacturers from Siemens. It specializes in implementing digital thread solutions that help clients connect engineering, manufacturing and automation across IT and operational technology, from product lifecycle management, simulation and digital twins to Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), industrial edge computing and cloud computing.

        

          

            
            
            
            
          

        

        

IndX’s clients are leading companies in industries including aerospace & defense, automotive, consumer goods, energy, high tech, industrial equipment, life sciences and utilities. It has a team of more than 650 professionals based in Italy, US, India, Germany, other European countries and Mexico.

        

Once the acquisition has been completed, IndX’s team and capabilities are expected to support the continued growth of the Accenture Siemens Business Group, a dedicated global business practice formed last year, which combines leading industrial technology with AI-enabled engineering and manufacturing capabilities.

        

“Accenture’s acquisition of IndX is a milestone for the Accenture Siemens Business Group,” said Tony Hemmelgarn, President and CEO of Siemens Digital Industries Software. “It brings proven skills in our industrial solutions for digital manufacturing, engineering, automation, digital twin and simulation, plus long-standing relationships with clients that apply them.”

        

“Together with Siemens, we develop industrial AI-enabled solutions that shorten engineering time to market, increase manufacturing efficiencies and strengthen the digital core for our clients,” added Vivek Kaushik, global lead of Accenture Siemens Business Group at Accenture. “IndX will strengthen the Accenture Siemens Business Group and help deliver on Accenture and Siemens’ shared ambition to scale these AI solutions.”

        

Following the completion of the acquisition, Accenture plans to establish two new Centers of Excellence for Siemens DI solutions in Italy and India. The centers will bring together professionals with expertise in industrial software and advanced digital technologies to help clients improve how they design products, run factories, and manage supply chains by combining industrial software, AI and digital engineering capabilities.

        

“Italy has a unique combination of manufacturing excellence, engineering capabilities and innovation talent,” said Teodoro Lio, Market Unit Lead of Accenture Italy. “By expanding our Siemens industrial software capabilities and creating a new Center of Excellence in Italy, we are strengthening an ecosystem that can help Italian industry become even more competitive at the global level, accelerate digital transformation, and create highly specialized skills and jobs for the country.”

        

Accenture will integrate IndX’s assets and services for other technologies into its respective business units.

        

Terms of the transaction were not disclosed. Completion of the acquisition is subject to customary closing conditions.

title: Accenture Life Trends 2027 Finds People Want Progress in an AI Era, but on Their Own Terms
snippet: Accenture today launched its 20th annual Life Trends 2027 report, finding that in the age of AI people are embracing technological and scientific progress while resisting the loss of control that can come with it.
fullText:
Consumers are exercising agency by using AI to search, create, and earn, but recoil from the synthetic sameness of digital experiences. They want medicine to help them live longer but are exhausted by the pressure to optimize every part of life. They value global convenience but increasingly expect companies to prove their worth locally. These are not inconsistencies but are expressions of the same demand: People want progress, but on their terms.

        

          

            
            
            
            
          

        

        

“If the internet made distribution instant, AI makes creation infinite. As this creates more things than can be possibly experienced, originality and quality will separate what’s worthy of attention,” said Nick Law, creative strategy and experience lead at Accenture Song. “The opportunity for brands is to use AI to power the “how" while talented humans determine the “why” with focused strategy and creative discernment."

        

Based on a survey of more than 28,000 people across 26 countries, approximately 100 in-depth consumer interviews and local insights from more than 40 teams worldwide, the report identifies five trends reshaping consumer behavior and challenging businesses to rethink how they create relevance and growth.

        

          

People seeking people: Content on the internet is becoming easier for machines to produce and harder for people to enjoy. Fifty percent of consumers globally say their feeds are becoming irrelevant, while 60% of people ages 18 to 24 say brands that use AI for content or advertising look lazy, careless and cheap. In response, people are looking for experiences that signal human effort and presence: distinctive voices, direct creator relationships, smaller communities, and time together offline. AI still has a place, but people want to choose that place. In an increasingly uncanny digital world of synthetic content, human presence is the ultimate signal of trust, making authentic connections more valuable than ever.

          

Reclaiming local: Global reach no longer guarantees local acceptance. Sixty-three percent of consumers say companies should earn the right to operate by creating local jobs. Decades of frictionless globalization pursuits are unraveling as nations, companies, and individuals actively renegotiate control of local far beyond simple consumer preferences. The scrutiny is extending to technology infrastructure, as communities question what data centers and other systems take in land, water, energy and data, and what they give in return. Local relevance is now a corporate strategy beyond simply the final mile of an invisible e-commerce system and is being built on proximity, reciprocity, and trust.

          

System override: Medicine is beginning to change not only how people manage illness, but what they believe their bodies can overcome. Seventy percent of consumers are more hopeful than ever that the health issues they care about most will be solved in their lifetime. Social proof is accelerating demand: 58% of people who know several others using weight-loss medication are open to trying it themselves, compared with 28% of those who know no one using it. As treatments begin to influence appetite, cravings and other drivers of behavior, their effects will not stop at healthcare but impact demand across food, retail, advertising, wellness and insurance.

          

Build it yourself: For many, one job, one skill and one source of income no longer feel secure enough. In the past year, 67% of consumers globally say they have made money beyond their main job. Over the next 12 months, 45% plan to learn a practical or manual skill to make money. People are already using platforms for income stacking, but now AI has been added as a powerful tool to widen what people believe they can do without formal training or institutional support: 15% have already used it to create a product or service to sell. As a new class of resourceful individuals actively break through friction to build their own solutions, forward-thinking businesses must determine how to empower this maker mindset rather than be bypassed by it.

          

Wellness burnout: No longer limited to basic health, wellness now spans every facet of life—from finance to relationships—bringing new metrics, protocols, and standards of failure to everyday living. Globally, 83% of people follow some form of health improvement or optimization routine, yet more than half find the effort exhausting. Forty-five percent swing between pushing themselves too hard and giving up completely. Online culture is raising the pressure, with mentions of terms such as “sleepmaxxing,” “looksmaxxing” and “moneymaxxing” rising 270% over the past year. The pursuit of wellness has become a lot of additional work. For many, it now feels like another performance review. Brands built on reminders of personal inadequacy risk wearing out the people they depend on.

        

        

“While technological acceleration is reshaping how businesses operate, consumer behavior holds equal weight in defining where they are headed,” said Ndidi Oteh, chief executive officer at Accenture Song. “These emerging behaviors are a vital counterweight and the ultimate compass for organizations trying to find relevance and prioritize what matters. When brands truly listen to how people are navigating choice, reclaiming place, and demanding real agency, they stop chasing short-term noise and start building deep, lasting value for the customer.”

        

To read this year’s Accenture Life Trends 2027 report, visit accenture.com/LifeTrends2027.

        

Research Methodology

The findings in this report draw on local behavioral research from more than 40 Accenture Song teams of designers, researchers, anthropologists and other specialists worldwide, combined with interviews with senior leaders and subject matter experts to shape the trends. We then conducted in-depth interviews with about 100 people across 11 countries; an online survey of 28,000 people across 26 countries to measure the prevalence and magnitude of each trend; netnographic analysis of public online discourse; and interviews with executives from major companies to test the trends and understand how organizations are responding.

title: Mondelēz International and Accenture Transform Order-to-Cash With AI
snippet: Mondelēz International and Accenture are collaborating to transform Mondelēz's end-to-end Order-to-Cash process through agentic AI, and integration of new technologies. The transformation is designed to simplify operations, reimagine the customer experience, and enhance customer financial performance. The collaboration is expected to reshape how the organizations work together, with outcomes serving as the primary measure of success.
fullText:
Order-to-Cash spans every stage from order placement through payment collection and plays a critical role in customer experience, revenue generation and cash flow. For Mondelēz, the process enables millions of transactions each year across customers, markets and distribution networks. For customers, a more streamlined Order-to-Cash process can mean quicker deliveries because it improves management, credit checks, fulfillment, invoicing, and collections.

        

          

            
            
            
            
          

        

        

By applying agentic AI across the end-to-end process, Mondelēz and Accenture are connecting customer service, supply chain and finance operations to streamline workflows, improve visibility and enable faster decision-making. The transformation is expected to accelerate payment collections, strengthen working capital performance and help teams resolve issues more quickly.

        

"Order-to-Cash is where customer demand becomes revenue, making it a critical driver of customer experience, cash flow and business performance day in and day out," said Filippo Catalano, chief information & digital officer, Mondelēz International. "Built on the digital foundation of our new global cloud ERP and powered by agentic AI on top of our process intelligence layer, we're transforming Order-to-Cash into a more connected, intelligent end-to-end flow that helps our teams work more efficiently, respond faster to customer needs and gain greater visibility into our operations. This transformation will help us improve service levels, strengthen our financial performance and create a more agile foundation for future growth."

        

"AI is creating new opportunities for Mondelēz to fundamentally reimagine how critical business processes operate, generate value and unlock greater returns from their operations," said Marco Ziegler, senior managing director and global client account lead for Mondelēz at Accenture. "Together with Mondelēz, we're transforming Order-to-Cash into a more connected, data-driven process that can accelerate cash collections, improve working capital, improve operational efficiency and deliver tangible business outcomes with measurable financial impact."

        

The initiative is expected to simplify day-to-day work by providing real-time insights across the Order-to-Cash process, improving accuracy, reducing costs and accelerating cash collections. Customer-facing teams will be better equipped to resolve issues faster, finance teams will have greater visibility into business performance, and leaders will have the insights needed to act more quickly. Beyond Order-to-Cash, the approach can be extended across other business functions to improve performance and support growth.

        

Sanjay Gurbuxani, global vice president, digital supply chain, Mondelēz International, added, “This collaboration marks a step change in how we operate—by embedding agentic AI into the heart of Order-to-Cash. We are not just improving a process, we are building the intelligent backbone for how Mondelēz serves customers and drives growth at scale.”
